key_insight: In layered soft porous media, matching the usual poroelastic timescale does not guarantee similar behavior: layering creates distinct localization and propagation of strain, flow, and solute transport.
engineering_relevance: This suggests that biological and engineered porous tissues can be tuned by architecture, not just bulk material properties, to control fluid transport and clearance.
method: Built a bilayer poromechanics model of a generic soft porous medium.
Matched poroelastic timescale across four layered configurations and one homogeneous reference.
Compared strain, fluid-flow, and solute-transport responses under periodic loading.
evidence_signal: The study uses a modeling comparison across four layered cases and a homogeneous case to show that identical poroelastic timescales still produce qualitatively different transport responses.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on a simplified bilayer model, so translating them to real tissues will require validation with more complex anatomy and parameter variability.
paper_title: Pulsatile poromechanics in layered soft media controls fluid flow and solute transport: from fundamentals to brain clearance
